International Graduate Applicants
Columbian College students and faculty are engaged in intellectual rigor that reaches beyond our classroom and labs to nations around the globe.
With international students comprising 28 percent of Columbian College’s total student enrollment, we take pride in the diversity of our campus and the degree to which our academic family participates in the worldwide circulation of ideas.
The application process for international applicants is the same as for domestic applicants, with the exception of a few additional requirements listed.
English Language Requirement
Graduate applicants who have not completed a post-secondary degree from a U.S. institution are required to submit official scores for TOEFL (Test of English as a Foreign Language), IELTS (International English Language Testing Service), Duolingo, or PTE (Pearson Test of English Academic), unless they meet an exemption indicated on the list below (English Language Test Exemptions). Official English scores may not be more than 2 years old from the time of application submission. We do not accept TOEFL MyBestScore.
We do not accept any document(s) other than official Duolingo, IELTS, PTE, or TOEFL English Language Test scores as proof of English Language proficiency. The George Washington University reserves the right to request proof of English proficiency from any applicant.
CCAS has two minimum English language proficiency requirements. Ensure you check your programs minimum requirements for admission.

Submitting English Language Scores
We only accept official English scores received directly from the testing agency.
TOEFL: Please send scores to George Washington University, institutional code 5246. We do not accept TOEFL Best Scores.
IELTS: Please send scores via the IELTS portal (e-delivery). We do not accept IELTS Indicator. You may need to provide the following information:
Account Name: George Washington University
Address: 1922 F Street NW Fourth Floor
City: Washington
State: DC
Zip Code: 20052
Some IELTS test center systems list an alternative address of 2121 I ("Eye") Street NW for the GWU account. You can use the GWU account associated with either address, and the e-delivery will be successful.
Duolingo: Please send scores directly through the Duolingo portal
PTE: Please send scores directly through the PTE portal
English for Academic Purposes (EAP)
Students who are admitted to a program that permits the lower English proficiency scores will need to take an English for Academic Purposes (EAP) course in the first semester. The particular course is determined using the Writing and Speaking scores and will be stipulated in the admission letter. There will be additional costs involved as the EAP course does not count towards the program requirements.
For more information, visit the EAP program website.
English Language Test Exemption
Exceptions to the English language proficiency policy will be granted if you have:
A degree (or will complete one before starting at GW) in which English is the language of instruction AND the official language of the country in which the university is located; or
A degree (or will complete one before starting at GW) from an institution that is accredited by a U.S. regional accrediting agency.
You do not have to apply for either waiver. Simply submit your application without the required scores. The CCAS Office of Graduate Studies will review your application and update the status of a waiver within 2 business days.

Documents Required for Form I-20
You are not required to submit I-20 or DS-2019 documentation during the initial application process. On your application for admission, you will simply be asked to indicate whether you will require an F-1 or J-1 visa to study in the U.S. We strongly recommend that you research U.S. visa requirements prior to applying to ensure you are familiar with the necessary steps.
If you are offered admission, GW will send you detailed instructions regarding the specific documentation you must submit to receive your I-20 or DS-2019 form. Alternatively you can visit our admitted students page for more information.
Health Insurance
All international students on an F-1 or J-1 visa are required to have adequate health insurance. As a result, all students will be automatically enrolled in the George Washington University plan. You may apply to opt-out of this plan providing you have your own insurance plan and it meets all the university's minimum requirements. More information can be found on the Student Health Center website.
